contents.name: Lemma 54.15.1: for a one-dimensional integral Noetherian scheme Y, the conditions (finite alteration / resolution / finite sequence of blowups in closed points ending regular / finite normalization) are equivalent; proof by the strictly decreasing system f_*O_X contains ... contains O_Y of coherent submodules

Lemma 54.15.1, factorization step: given a finite resolution X -> Y and a singular closed point y, the ideal sheaf m_y O_X is invertible because the local rings of X are discrete valuation rings, so the universal property of the blowup gives X -> Y_i
Lemma 54.15.1, strictness: each blowup Y_i -> Y_{i-1} is not an isomorphism because m_{y_{i-1}} is not invertible at a singular point
Lemma 54.15.1, stabilization: the increasing sequence of coherent submodules of the fixed finite resolution stabilizes by Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.10.1

Lemma 54.15.2: for Y inside an arbitrary Noetherian ambient X, the corresponding blowup sequence makes the strict transform of Y regular, because the strict transform is the blowup of Y in the corresponding point (Divisors, Lemma 31.34.2)
Invariant (54.15.2.1): m_p(Y cap Z) = length_{O_{X,p}}(O_{Y cap Z,p}), finite by the dimension-one hypothesis on Y
Lemma 54.15.3: if O_{Y,p} is regular, then Y' -> Y is an isomorphism, Y' meets E in one point q with m_q(Y' cap E) = 1, and m_q(Y' cap Z') < m_p(Y cap Z); complete chart proof in A[m/x_1] read

Lemma 54.15.4: finitely many integral one-dimensional closed subschemes with finite normalization have pairwise disjoint regular strict transforms after finitely many point blowups, by maximizing m_p(Y_i cap Y_j) and using 54.15.3
Lemma 54.15.5: on a regular surface, a proper closed subscheme becomes an effective Cartier divisor after finitely many point blowups (uses Divisors Lemma 31.16.8 and Lemma 54.4.1)

Lemma 54.15.6: on a regular surface, if every one-dimensional irreducible component satisfies the finite-normalization condition, finitely many point blowups make the inverse image an effective Cartier divisor supported on a strict normal crossings divisor

Lemma 54.15.1 relies on Lemma 54.13.1 (finite alteration implies finite normalization) and Lemma 33.17.2 (tag 0AB7) for the finiteness of the resolution; this batch uses the equivalent proper-quasi-finite criterion (Stacks 37.44.1, tag 02LS, and the published library item thm-proper-quasi-finite-is-finite) instead

Lemma 54.15.3 and 54.15.6 use Divisors, Lemma 31.34.2 (tag 080E, strict transform is the blowup) and Lemma 31.33.5/31.33.7; the library items thm-blowup-closed-immersion-transform-universal and thm-blowup-effective-cartier-divisor-isomorphism supply these

Lemma 54.15.6 uses that the exceptional divisor of a point blowup of a regular surface is a regular curve (Divisors, Lemma 54.3.1, tag 0AGQ); the library item lem-blowup-of-closed-point-of-regular-surface-is-regular proves this over arbitrary residue fields by the two standard charts

Lemma 54.15.5's auxiliary input Lemma 54.4.1 (making a point-supported ideal invertible by blowups) is not needed in this pair's reduced-curve scope: a reduced curve on a regular surface is already an effective Cartier divisor, so the total transform is Cartier from the start
contents.reason: The pair resolves reduced curves (pure dimension one); non-reduced or embedded-point parts of the general 54.15.6 statement and its Lemma 54.4.1 machinery are deliberately not built and not claimed.

contents.name: Alterations and the general resolution-of-singularities formalism of Section 54.13 (Lemma 54.13.1) are not used; only the finite-normalization hypothesis and the equivalence with point-blowup regularization enter
contents.reason: The commissioned curve and embedded-SNC theorems assume finite normalization and prove point-blowup regularization, coherent-algebra stabilization and contact descent. Lemma 54.13.1 instead derives finite normalization from a regular alteration, including for dimension-one curves; this converse alteration implication and the full alteration/resolution equivalence are not claimed or used by this pair.

contents.name: Lemma 41.21.2: a strict normal crossings divisor is equivalent to a reduced effective Cartier divisor whose components are effective Cartier divisors and whose finite scheme-theoretic intersections are regular of codimension equal to the number of factors
Lemma 41.21.2, used at the end of the embedded-resolution argument to identify the terminal configuration (regular components, pairwise transverse, no triple points) with an SNC divisor

contents.name: Lemma 37.44.1 is the scheme-level input for the finiteness of the point blowup of a one-dimensional integral scheme and of its exceptional fibre; the library's published thm-proper-quasi-finite-is-finite is the local supplier

Varieties Lemma 33.17.2 is how Stacks 54.15.1 obtains finiteness of the resolution and of the intermediate blowups over a one-dimensional Noetherian base; the local proof replaces it by the proper-quasi-finite criterion, with the exceptional-fibre dimension computed by the Hilbert-Samuel theorem

contents.name: Section 28.4.4, last paragraph (p. 781): if the blowup beta: C' -> C of a reduced projective curve over a field at a point p is an isomorphism, then O_{C,p} is a regular local ring of dimension one (the maximal ideal is principal)

Section 28.4.4 (pp. 781-782): termination of blowups at singular points of a reduced projective curve over a field by strict decrease of the arithmetic genus, with the O-connected (Stein) comparison and Exercise 28.4.E (affine O-connected implies isomorphism)
contents.reason: Vakil proves the field case for reduced projective curves using arithmetic genus, a narrower scope than this pair's arbitrary Noetherian regular surfaces; the design row states explicitly that V25 28.4.4/Ex. 28.4.E cannot close the broader claim, and the page keeps the Stacks 54.15 route for the general statements. The section remains the independent treatment for the finite-type-over-a-field specialization illustrated on the B page.

contents.name: Lemma 54.15.3, chart computation for a node: two distinct tangent directions give two distinct points of the exceptional curve, each of multiplicity 1, so one blowup separates the branches

Lemma 54.15.3, chart computation for a cusp: multiplicity two with a single tangent direction gives one point of multiplicity 1 on the exceptional curve; the strict transform is the regular normalization
Lemma 54.15.4 and 54.15.1: the finite-normalization hypothesis is only the input guaranteeing termination of point blowups; it does not make the curve regular before blowing up

The affine charts, multiplicities and delta invariants of the two projective-completion computations are supplied locally (batch-2 delta machinery and the published Hilbert-Samuel/defect items); the Stacks text is the source of the underlying chart computations
